result.rationale: The diff at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. These are not dynamic keys — they evaluate to identical literal strings (e.g. '[ZodString]'), so the intended 'any number property = expiry' and 'allow other properties' validation never applies. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, fields like refresh_token and expires_in would be stripped from the parsed data, and the code then assigns the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh to

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to define dynamic keys via computed properties `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS this does not create a catch-all/dynamic key; it evaluates to a single literal property name (stringified object), so it won’t validate real token fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`. Also, since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default and the schema doesn’t use `.passthrough()`/`catchall`, any extra fields would be stripped rather than preserved. This is a concrete correctness defect in the diff-introduced schema/validation logic.
